title: Human IFN-alpha2- and PD-L1-overexpressing T cells (ap-T cells) inhibit graft-versus-host disease but retain anti-leukemia activity in mice
description: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a major barrier to successful allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT). Systemic immunosuppression used to control GVHD often compromises anti-leukemia immunity. To address this, we engineered human CD4+ T cells from a single donor's Buffy coat (New York Blood Center) via lentiviral transduction with either an empty vector (v-T cells) or constructs encoding PD-L1 and IFN-alpha (ap-T cells). In a xenogeneic GVHD model using NOD/SCID/IL2Rg-/- (NSG) mice, ap-T cells suppressed pathogenic T cell responses while retaining the ability to eliminate human leukemia xenografts. To dissect the molecular mechanisms, PD-L1+ ap-T cells and v-T cells were FACS-sorted on day 12 of in vitro culture, stimulated with PMA/ionomycin (2 hours), and subjected to bulk RNA-seq analysis. Separately, PD-L1- conventional T cells (conv-T cells) were isolated via FACS 5 days after co-culture with ap-T cells, followed by PMA/ionomycin stimulation (2 hours) for RNA-seq. This study characterizes the suppressive function of ap-T cells and their mechanism of inhibiting PD-L1- conv-T cells, advancing insights into engineered T cell-mediated immune regulation.

attributes: Human T cells were isolated from Buffy coat obtained from the New York Blood Center (NYBC). CD4 T cells were subsequently activated, engineered via lentiviral infection and sorted in Dr. Yi Zhang’s lab at the Center for Discovery and Innovation, Hackensack Meridian Health.
